h1: The 6 Best Dehumidifiers Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six dehumidifiers under $300, compared on room coverage, tank size, drain hose options and features for bedrooms and basements.
summary: The AEOCKY is the strongest dehumidifier here, with 5,500 square feet of listed coverage, Energy Star certification and 80 pints per day, though you should confirm its price. The Kesnos covers 2,000 square feet with a continuous drain hose. The KeepGlad, ToLife and NineSky handle 1,000 square foot rooms, and the TABYIK bundles closet boxes.
intro: Coverage figures on dehumidifier listings flatter the machine. A 1,000 square foot rating describes a room that is a little damp on a mild day, not a basement in August, and a unit pushed past its rating runs without stopping while the humidity barely moves. Treat the number as a ceiling for easy conditions and size up for any space that smells musty.

Tank size is the other half of the story, because a small tank means a trip to the sink once a day. Eight dehumidifiers were reviewed and six ranked on spec sheets: listed coverage, tank size, drain hose, timers and sleep modes. The 80-pint AEOCKY sits in a higher bracket than the rest, so check its live price against your $300 limit before you buy.

products.name: AEOCKY 5500 Sq.Ft Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 Dehumidifier Max 80Pint/D
products.verdict: Energy Star certified with 5,500 square feet of listed coverage and 80 pints per day.
products.description:
The AEOCKY is the heavyweight of the group. It lists 5,500 square feet of coverage, an 80 pints-per-day maximum capacity and Energy Star certification, far beyond the single-room models that follow. Capacity in pints per day is the real work rate: it says how much water the machine can pull from the air daily, and 80 is a different class from the small tank units.

It ranks first on capacity, but it sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, so confirm the live price is under $300 before committing. The Kesnos below costs less and covers less.

Buy it for a big basement or whole-house drying. The caveat is size and price: it is overkill for a single bedroom, where a 1,000 square foot unit will do, and it may draw more power than a small room needs.
products.skipIf: You only have a bedroom to dry.

products.name: Kesnos 34 Pin Dehumidifiers for Home and Basements, Dehumidifiers For Bedroom with Continuous Drain Hose For 2000 Sq. Ft, 24H Timer, Child Lock and Auto Defrost for Basement, Office and Bathroom
products.verdict: 2,000 square feet of coverage with a continuous drain hose and a 24-hour timer.
products.description:
The Kesnos solves the two annoyances of a damp room. It lists 2,000 square feet of coverage, the largest of the small-footprint units here, and a continuous drain hose so the tank never needs emptying. A 24-hour timer, child lock and auto defrost round out the controls.

It ranks second behind the AEOCKY because coverage and continuous drainage handle the biggest problems in wet spaces. The 1,000 square foot models below are fine for bedrooms but not for basements, where they run constantly.

Buy it for a basement or large living area with a drain nearby. The caveat is plumbing: continuous draining needs a floor drain or sink, and the unit is larger than the bedroom models. If no drain is close, the tank still works, but you give up the main advantage.
products.skipIf: You only need to dry a small bedroom.

products.name: KeepGlad Dehumidifier, 98OZ Dehumidifiers for Home(1000sq.ft), Humidity Display Dehumidifier for Basement Bathroom Bedroom, Auto Shut Off, Washable Filter, Drain Hose, Timer, 7 Ambient Lights, White
products.verdict: A 98 oz tank with a humidity display and washable filter for 1,000 square feet.
products.description:
The KeepGlad is built for bedrooms and small apartments. It lists 1,000 square feet of coverage, a 98 oz tank, a humidity display, a washable filter, a drain hose option and a timer, in the $50 to $100 bucket. The display shows room humidity at a glance, which tells you when to run it and when to stop.

It ranks third because it covers half the area of the Kesnos, but the readout is a genuine advantage. You trade coverage for monitoring and a lower price.

Pick it for a bedroom, bathroom or small apartment. The caveat is rating: 1,000 square feet assumes moderate dampness, so it is not meant for a very wet space such as a basement after rain. Use the drain hose if you do not want to carry the tank each morning.

products.name: ToLife Dehumidifier, 1000 Sq Ft 95 oz Tank with Sleep Mode, Auto Shutoff
products.verdict: A 95 oz tank with a sleep mode and auto shutoff.
products.description:
The ToLife is for light sleepers. It lists 1,000 square feet of coverage, a 95 oz tank, a sleep mode and auto shutoff, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A sleep mode exists to reduce noise at night, which matters if the unit sits beside the bed, and auto shutoff stops it when the tank is full.

It ranks fourth because the listing is shorter than the KeepGlad's: it names no humidity display and no drain hose, so you have less feedback and less flexibility. You gain a night-friendly mode in exchange.

Pick it if noise bothers you in a bedroom. The caveat is routine: the tank still needs emptying, and the listing does not publish decibels, so you cannot compare its quiet claim with other models. Check owner comments about overnight noise.

products.name: TABYIK Dehumidifiers for Home, 101oz Dehumidifier & 2pack Rechargeable Dehumidifying Boxes - Auto Shut Off Auto Defrost Quiet Dehumidifiers for Bathroom Room Wardrobe Closet Trailer RV
products.verdict: A 101 oz tank plus two rechargeable dehumidifying boxes.
products.description:
The TABYIK is a bundle. It lists a 101 oz tank, auto shutoff and auto defrost, and adds two rechargeable dehumidifying boxes for closets and wardrobes. The tank is the largest in the group, so you empty it less often, and the boxes protect small spaces where a full unit does not fit.

It ranks fifth because the listing shows no coverage figure, so fitting it to a room is guesswork. The boxes are a useful extra, but they need recharging, and they do not replace a proper dehumidifier for a damp room.

Pick it for a bedroom plus closet where the main unit has to work hard but not for long. The caveat is the missing coverage rating, so ask the seller for the room size it is intended for, and do not use it for a wet basement.
products.skipIf: You need a stated coverage figure.

products.name: NineSky Dehumidifiers for Home, 1000 Sq.Ft Dehumidifier with 95oz Water Tank, Quiet Dehumidifier for Basement Bathroom Bedroom with 7-Color Ambient Light & Auto Shut Off, White
products.verdict: A 95 oz unit with a 7-colour ambient light.
products.description:
The NineSky pairs a 95 oz tank and 1,000 square feet of coverage with a seven-color ambient light, in the $50 to $100 bucket. The core dehumidifier is conventional, with an auto shutoff and a quiet claim, and the lamp is an add-on.

It ranks sixth because the light is cosmetic next to the display and drain features on the KeepGlad. It does nothing for drying, and a feature list that leads with mood lighting suggests the priorities of the design.

Pick it for a nightstand where you want a small glow and a modest bedroom unit. The caveat is that the light adds nothing to performance. Skip it if you want practical features such as a drain hose or a humidity readout, which the KeepGlad includes.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms where mood lighting is welcome.

whatMatters.detail: Coverage is the square footage a dehumidifier is rated for, and ratings assume moderate dampness. For wet spaces, pick a unit rated higher than the room, since an undersized machine runs nonstop. Check the sq ft number in the title, and compare it with your real room size, not the whole home, since the unit only treats one open space.

Tank size sets how long before you must empty it, and ounces here range up to 101. A bigger tank means fewer trips, but a full tank is heavy. Check the number in the listing and use a drain hose if you hate emptying, since a hose removes the chore entirely and the unit can run for days.

A hose lets water flow to a drain, so you never empty the tank. It needs a nearby drain or sink and gravity, so the hose runs downhill. Look for the words drain hose or continuous drain in the bullets, and check that the unit sits higher than the drain, because the water will not flow uphill.

Auto shutoff stops the unit when the tank is full, and auto defrost prevents ice buildup on the coils in cooler rooms. Both protect the machine and save you from overflow. Check for them in the listing, especially if you plan to run the unit overnight or while you are out, since spilled water ruins floors.

Noise matters in bedrooms, and sleep modes help, but few listings publish decibels. Look for a numeric figure before trusting a quiet claim, and check owner comments about overnight sound. A unit that cycles constantly in an undersized room will be louder than a larger one, so size matters for sleep too.

faq.q: What size dehumidifier do I need?
faq.a: Match the listed coverage to your room and go higher for damp spaces. A 1,000 square foot model suits a bedroom, the Kesnos suits 2,000 square feet, and the AEOCKY suits large basements and whole-house jobs where its price fits.

Buying a small unit for a wet basement. It will run constantly and still struggle, so choose the Kesnos or AEOCKY for large or damp spaces rather than a bedroom model, and check the room is closed to outside air.

faq.q: Is the Kesnos worth it over the KeepGlad?
faq.a: Yes for large or wet spaces, thanks to its 2,000 square feet and continuous drain. For bedrooms, the KeepGlad is enough and adds a humidity display that shows when the room is dry enough to switch off.

faq.q: How do I use a drain hose?
faq.a: Connect the hose to the outlet and run it downhill to a drain or sink. Keep the hose free of kinks so water can flow out freely, and check the connection for leaks after an hour.

Wash the filter and empty the tank regularly. The KeepGlad lists a washable filter, and all of these benefit from a clean intake so airflow stays strong and the machine does not work harder than needed. Rinse it monthly in damp seasons.

Models with auto shutoff, like the ToLife, KeepGlad and NineSky, are designed to stop when the tank is full. The Kesnos with a drain hose can run without stopping because the water drains away, but still watch the first overnight run.

finalTake: Choose the AEOCKY for a whole-house or large basement job if the price fits, or the Kesnos for 2,000 square feet and a drain hose. For bedrooms, the KeepGlad has a humidity display, the ToLife has a sleep mode, and the TABYIK adds closet boxes but states no coverage. The NineSky is the cosmetic choice.
